Commentary.Commentary: In all readiness for the action to take over now! The two umpires are out and are followed by Bangladesh team spreading across the field. Kraigg Brathwaite and Mikyle Louis are the openers striding out to bat for the hosts while Taskin Ahmed has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play says the umpire and here we go!
... THIRD INNINGS ...

West Indies, on the other hand, will be thrilled with their bowling performance. Alzarri Joseph delivered fiery spells to claim three wickets, while Jayden Seales, Kemar Roach and Shamar Joseph combined to share four more, showcasing a disciplined and relentless effort. Justin Greaves chipped in with two wickets as well. With a hefty 181-run lead, West Indies are poised to come out with positivity, aiming to post a significant total and push for a dominant result. For Bangladesh, it’s all about a turnaround with the ball. They’ll need to give everything to restrict the hosts to a manageable score. West Indies’ reply is coming up shortly!

Chasing a daunting trail of 450 runs, Bangladesh needed big partnerships and monumental knocks, but those eluded them. While they showed grit and determination, their overly defensive approach limited their scoring opportunities. Mominul Haque continued his fine run against the Windies, scoring his third Test fifty against them. Solid starts from Litton Da and Jaker Ali added hope, but none could convert their efforts into the kind of innings the team desperately needed. The tail wagged just enough to avoid the follow-on, which was a small but crucial positive.

Right then, news from the middle - Bangladesh have declared their innings at 269/9, handing West Indies a lead of 181 runs! A bold and unexpected decision, leaving many surprised, but it signals Bangladesh's intent to shake things up in this game. Now, it’s over to the West Indies, who will stride out with the bat to capitalize on this opportunity and extend their advantage. How pivotal could this declaration turn out to be? Only time will tell!

Jayden Seales is in for a chat. He says as a group they tried to pitch the ball in the right areas and make the batters play. Adds that he tried to set Mominul Haque by switching his angles and trying to make him play and the one he tried to nip back in worked for him well. Talks about his sharp catch and says fielding is crucial and he tries to put in that extra effort to contribute to the side and is really happy that catch stuck. Appreciates the rest of the bowlers who showed great intent and kept building pressure.

West Indies, on the other hand, have been relentless and composed, which is why they hold the upper hand in this game. Their approach has been clinical, first with the bat, and then with the pace attack, spearheaded by Alzarri Joseph, delivering when it mattered most despite facing occasional pressure. Their immediate goal will be to clean up the final Bangladeshi wicket quickly and get back to batting. With two full days left in the match, the hosts have the chance to press the accelerator, pile on a commanding total, and set up a push for victory. There’s everything to play for, and both teams will be eager to make their mark. Brace up for another thrilling day of red-ball cricket as the action resumes shortly!

Bangladesh showed glimpses of fight in their batting effort, with Mominul Haque, Litton Das and Jaker Ali getting off to promising starts. However, what they truly needed was someone to anchor the innings and convert those starts into a significant knock which didn't happen and has left them reeling in this contest. With just one wicket remaining, they’ll be hoping to chip away at the deficit and add as many runs as possible before heading out to bowl. That said, turning this game around will require everything to fall perfectly into place for the visitors. They’ll need intent, precision, and a bit of luck with the ball to make amends. For now, they are staring down the barrel and must find a way to mount a spirited comeback.

Hello and welcome back to Day 4 of this intriguing first Test between West Indies and Bangladesh, coming to you from the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in Antigua! With Bangladesh trailing by 181 runs and down to their final wicket, the game is firmly in West Indies' control. By the end of today’s play, we should have a much clearer picture of where this game will head, though the hosts will undoubtedly start the day in the driver's seat.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from an action-packed Day 3 of this first Test. West Indies are in the driver's seat, but Bangladesh will not go down without a fight here. Day 4 will begin at 2 pm GMT, but you can join us early for all he build-up. Cheers!

Alzarri Joseph is up for a quick chat. He says that the wicket was slow and they bowled in partnerships. Adds that they had a plan and they stuck to that and thus got the results. All plans worked today. Mentions that they have Kemar Roach in the side and thus he won't say that he is the leader because Roach has more experience. Concludes that the team will have to be passionate in the remaining couple of days to win this one.

West Indies kept the pressure on in the and were rewarded when Alzarri Joseph's short-ball strategy dismissed skipper Mehidy Hasan. But Jaker Ali stood firm, battling alongside Taijul Islam to add a vital 50-plus partnership, edging Bangladesh closer to 250. Ali’s gritty half-century ended while trying to accelerate, and Taijul fell to Alzarri shortly before that. Justin Greaves picked up a couple of crucial wickets and also registered his best Test figures, which he can still improve on Day 4. The lower order scraped past the follow-on mark, aided by some missed chances from the Windies. As the light faded, Bangladesh clung on, surviving a relentless final session.

Resuming at 105/3 after Lunch, Litton Das and Mominul Haque blended caution with aggression, keeping Bangladesh in the fight. Mominul’s gritty knock of 50 off 116 balls, his third fifty against the Windies, ended right after reaching the milestone. Litton, steady during his 76-ball stay, fell to an inside edge off Shamar Joseph, leaving the visitors in a spot of bother. Skipper Mehidy Hasan weathered a fiery spell from Alzarri Joseph before steadying the ship with Jaker Ali, who joined him after Litton’s dismissal. At Tea, Miraz remained unbeaten on 22, with Jaker on 5, as Bangladesh looked to rebuild amidst relentless pressure.

Bangladesh showed immense grit from the outset, frustrating the Windies pacers despite a few lucky escapes. West Indies, holding a commanding lead, struck just before the first hour as Kemar Roach delivered a vital breakthrough. Alzarri and Shamar Joseph bowled with fire but lacked consistency. After Shahadat Hossain’s dismissal, Litton Das brought positive intent, joining forces with Mominul Haque’s determined resistance to take the total past 100 and end the first session unscathed reducing the lead to 345 runs.

SESSION SUMMARY - 104 runs and 4 wickets in 30 overs! Day 3 is called a 'Moving Day' for a reason and this Test has moved in favour of the West Indies massively. Shamar Joseph and Jayden Seales claimed a wicket each in the session, keeping West Indies in control. Join us shortly for the post-tea session as it will tell us largely about the game's outcome! Stay Tuned as we start the final session at 7 pm GMT.

Bangladesh skipper Mehidy Hasan Miraz endured a challenging start as Alzarri Joseph relentlessly tested him. However, Miraz found his footing and steadied the innings alongside Jaker Ali Anik, who joined him after Litton's dismissal. At tea, Miraz is unbeaten on 22, with Jaker Ali on 5.

Resuming at 105/3 after lunch, Litton Das and Mominul Haque adopted a balanced approach, mixing caution with occasional attacking strokes. Mominul showcased resilience to bring up his third fifty against the West Indies but fell immediately after, scoring 50 off 116 balls. Litton Das, after a composed 76-ball stay, was undone by an inside edge off Shamar Joseph.

West Indies made their first breakthrough just before the first hour, with Kemar Roach delivering the crucial wicket. Both Alzarri and Shamar Joseph bowled with intent, posing tough challenges but struggling with consistency. After Shahadat Hossain’s dismissal, Litton Das walked in with positive intent, complementing Mominul Haque’s steady resolve as the duo saw off the remainder of the session without further damage and taking the total over the 100-run mark. Bangladesh will aim to pick up the scoring rate in the next session, while the hosts will look to break into the lower middle order. Join us at 4:40 PM GMT to catch all the action!

SESSION SUMMARY - 65 runs and 1 wicket in 25 overs! Bangladesh displayed remarkable resilience from the very start of the session, successfully frustrating the Windies pacers. Commentary.Commentary: Here we go! The Umpires and the players walk out to take the stage for the start of Day 3 of this first Test Match of the series. It's Shahadat Hossain and Mominul Haque, the overnight batters for Bangladesh taking guard and Alzarri Joseph has the cherry in hand for the West Indies. Let's Play!

PITCH REPORT! Sir Curtley Ambrose and Samuel Badree analyze the pitch conditions and emphasize its potential for fast bowlers. They observe that the surface remains hard and placid despite a few slight cracks. Ambrose believes the morning session will offer opportunities for fast bowlers to strike early if they adopt an attacking approach. Badree concurs, highlighting the possibility of early wickets on this track.

As Day 3 dawns, the battle will likely intensify. For Bangladesh, survival and consolidation are key as they seek to avoid a collapse and edge closer to the hosts' imposing total. The West Indies bowlers, on the other hand, will aim to capitalize on the momentum and make further breakthroughs to maintain their dominance. All eyes will be on how the Bangladeshi batters handle the relentless Windies attack and whether they can mount a significant resistance. Stay tuned as the action unfolds on what promises to be another thrilling day of Test cricket!

The Bangladeshi bowlers had moments of brilliance but struggled to contain the West Indies middle and lower order. Taskin Ahmed and Hasan Mahmud were the pick of the bowlers, with Hasan bagging 3/87. However, their efforts fell short of dismantling the resilient Windies batting lineup. In response, Bangladesh faced a daunting task in their first innings. The visitors suffered early setbacks, losing both their openers by the close of play. By stumps, Bangladesh was reeling at 40/2, trailing by a mammoth 410 runs. With the West Indies bowlers already making inroads, the onus now lies on the Bangladeshi middle order to steady the ship and carve out a path to a competitive total.

West Indies concluded Day 2 in commanding fashion. Resuming their innings at 250/6, the hosts rode on Justin Greaves' magnificent maiden Test century, an innings marked by patience and grit, as he remained unbeaten on 115. Greaves received vital support from the experienced Kemar Roach, who chipped in with a valuable 47, frustrating the Bangladeshi bowlers in a 140-run partnership for the eighth wicket. The West Indies declared their innings at 450/9 after 144.1 overs, setting a formidable target for the visitors to chase.

Hello and a warm welcome to everyone joining us here today. The third day of the first Test at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium, North Sound, Antigua, is set to begin with both West Indies and Bangladesh striving to assert their dominance in this crucial encounter. After two days of compelling cricket, the stage is set for another exciting day as Bangladesh faces an uphill task to close the gap against a towering West Indies total.
... DAY 3, FIRST SESSION ...

Right then, that is it from an exciting Day 2 of this first Test. As we move into the 'Moving Day', West Indies hold a significant lead of 410 runs, and Bangladesh needs to do a lot more to make a game out of this one. Day 3 will begin at 2 pm GMT, but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Kemar Roach is up for a quick chat. He reflects on the day's play, expressing satisfaction with the recovery after losing two quick wickets. He highlights the plan to build partnerships and surpass 350, crediting the acceleration for the team’s strong total. Roach shares his camaraderie with Justin Greaves, emphasizing their shared understanding as teammates and friends. Praising Greaves’ maiden Test century, Roach reveals his long-standing belief in Greaves’ talent and hopes he continues to excel for the West Indies.

The Windies declared on a commanding 450/9, with Justin Greaves standing tall on a magnificent unbeaten 115. Jayden Seales and Shamar Joseph added quick late runs, setting the stage for their bowlers. Bangladesh’s openers started cautiously, fending off fiery pace spells, but Seales broke through, dismissing Zakir Hasan just as he found rhythm. Mikyle Louis dropped a sitter to give Zakir’s partner a lifeline on 5, but Alzarri Joseph’s searing delivery ended Mahmudul Hasan Joy's stay soon after. Under pressure, Shahadat Hossain and Mominul Haque dug deep, showing grit to survive until Stumps and keep Bangladesh in the fight.

West Indies showed grit in the second session, adding 79 runs in 29 overs as Justin Greaves and Kemar Roach frustrated Bangladesh early on. A costly missed edge off Taskin Ahmed denied them Greaves’ wicket, and the duo kept the visitors at bay. Hasan Mahmud finally broke the massive 140-run stand, clean-bowling Roach for a valiant 47, but not before Greaves celebrated a maiden Test century pushing the total over 400, earning roaring applause from teammates and fans alike.

Bangladesh started on the front foot but just like Day 1, faded away as the session progressed. Hasan Mahmud struck early, removing Joshua Da Silva in the first over and adding Alzarri Joseph soon after, igniting hopes for Bangladesh to restrict the Windies under 300. But Justin Greaves stood firm, anchoring the innings with steady support from Kemar Roach. While Bangladesh shuffled their bowlers and Mehidy Hasan and Taijul Islam kept things tight, clear breakthroughs remained eluded.

SESSION SUMMARY - 75 runs and 3 wickets in 25.1 overs! At the end of Day 2, the West Indies firmly hold the reins, boasting a mountain of runs and plenty of time to push for victory. Their batters set the tone with a stellar performance, and the bowlers backed it up with fiery intent. For Bangladesh, it’s a familiar story of struggle on this ground, and they now face an uphill battle. Only something extraordinary can reignite their hopes and keep this contest alive!

Umpire Kumar Dharmasena takes one more light reading, and this time it looks like it has gone over the reading that was taken on Day 1. So, that will be STUMPS ON DAY 2! Once again, we did lose a few overs due to a slight rain delay and bad light, but the game has moved at a good pace.
